name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that appears immediately on keyboard navigation. This ensures keyboard users can see where they are without extra clutter, meeting WCAG 2.2 Level AA. The trade-off is a slight visual shift for mouse users, but it’s minimal and improves usability for everyone.

name: Reader
text: A single high-contrast ring risks creating a visual "siren" that pulls attention away from the task, especially for users with cognitive disabilities or ADHD. Instead, use a subtle but visible focus indicator that adapts to the user’s motion preferences—like reduced motion or touch-first—so it’s always present but never jarring. Settle it with user testing: if sighted keyboard users can’t track focus within 3 seconds, or if any participant reports distraction, the design fails.
